high_risk_moment: AI generates the initial urgency-tier recommendation immediately after symptom intake, before the triage nurse reviews it
stakeholder: Patients from groups whose symptoms have historically been under-documented or under-escalated in clinical records
harm_description: If the model is tuned on historical triage or EHR data that reflects unequal past care, as Optum's Impact Pro reflected unequal past spending, it can systematically recommend a lower urgency tier for these patients even when their symptoms are equally severe, delaying their access to care.
existing_controls: none documented yet; the deterministic red-flag keyword engine only catches explicit emergency terms, not subtler group-level under-triage
proposed_controls: Remove cost/utilization-style proxy features from training data; require a subgroup performance evaluation (age, sex, self-reported demographic group, language) before every release; run new releases in shadow mode against nurse triage first
human_oversight: A triage nurse reviews every AI-recommended tier below 'urgent' during the pilot and can escalate immediately by phone; nurses currently do not see subgroup bias metrics, only the individual case
monitoring_metric: Nurse-upgrade (under-triage correction) rate broken out by self-reported demographic group, weekly
trigger_threshold: Any subgroup's upgrade rate is more than 5 percentage points above the overall average for two consecutive weeks
response_action: Pause AI urgency recommendations for the affected symptom category, route those cases to human-only triage, and open a bias investigation before re-enabling

high_risk_moment: The model classifies an early sepsis or rapidly-deteriorating symptom pattern as non-urgent because real-world sensitivity is lower than reported validation performance
stakeholder: Patients with early sepsis or fast-deteriorating conditions using the intake chatbot
harm_description: As with the Epic Sepsis Model's 33% real-world sensitivity versus its reported 0.76-0.83 AUC, a triage model can miss early deterioration signs and recommend routine scheduling instead of urgent escalation, delaying life-saving treatment.
existing_controls: A deterministic red-flag keyword list catches explicit emergency terms only
proposed_controls: Independent external validation of sensitivity, specificity, and AUC on this pilot's own patient population before go-live; mandatory nurse call-back within a fixed window for any borderline case; ongoing shadow monitoring against confirmed ED and hospital outcomes
human_oversight: The nurse reviews and can override every recommendation in the pilot scope, sees the model's rationale text, and has time, targeted under 20 minutes, to call the patient back before any non-urgent path is finalized
monitoring_metric: Sensitivity and false-negative rate for confirmed urgent-care outcomes, sampled weekly against ED and hospital records
trigger_threshold: Any confirmed missed-urgent case, or measured sensitivity falls more than 10 points below the validated baseline in a rolling 30-day sample
response_action: Immediately pause automated urgency recommendations for the affected symptom category, notify the Clinical AI Safety Officer and independent reviewer, and require re-validation before resuming

high_risk_moment: Nurses receive AI urgency recommendations throughout their shift, including frequent low-confidence or borderline flags
stakeholder: Telehealth triage nurses using the AI recommendation console
harm_description: As STAT News reported for Epic's sepsis alerts, frequent false or low-value alerts can cause alert fatigue, making nurses less likely to carefully review any given AI recommendation, including a true urgent case.
existing_controls: None yet; alert volume and nurse response time are not currently monitored
proposed_controls: Cap and monitor daily alert volume per nurse; tune the confidence threshold before go-live; give nurses a one-click 'low value alert' feedback control that feeds back into model tuning
human_oversight: The supervising clinical lead reviews weekly nurse feedback and can pause the recommendation feature for retuning, but does not yet have a real-time alert-fatigue dashboard
monitoring_metric: Median nurse response/review time per AI recommendation and weekly 'low value alert' feedback rate
trigger_threshold: Median review time drops below 15 seconds, or low-value feedback exceeds 20% of alerts, for one week
response_action: Retune or reduce the alert threshold, retrain nurses on the escalation protocol, and review a sample of recently reviewed cases for missed true positives

high_risk_moment: A patient with disordered-eating or weight-related symptoms interacts with the intake chatbot's general wellness or lifestyle guidance content
stakeholder: Patients vulnerable to disordered eating who enter weight- or diet-related symptoms
harm_description: As with NEDA's Tessa chatbot, generic calorie-counting or weight-loss guidance surfaced to a person with disordered-eating risk factors, without clinical-content review, can worsen an eating disorder rather than support safe care.
existing_controls: General wellness/lifestyle content library has not yet been reviewed specifically for eating-disorder safety
proposed_controls: Route any disordered-eating-risk keywords straight to a human counselor referral instead of any automated diet or weight content; require a clinical content review board to approve all wellness-adjacent scripted content before release
human_oversight: No automated wellness content is currently reviewed case-by-case by a clinician before being shown; only emergency red-flag terms get an immediate human handoff today
monitoring_metric: Rate of sessions containing disordered-eating-risk keywords that are routed to a human counselor referral versus shown any diet or weight content
trigger_threshold: Any confirmed instance of automated diet, weight, or calorie content shown after a disordered-eating-risk keyword
response_action: Immediately disable the wellness/lifestyle content module for that keyword category, notify the Clinical Content Safety Reviewer, and require content board re-approval before restoring it
